races.title: State House, District 59
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Alan Branson
cands.bio: Republican from Greensboro who owns a family trucking business. Served on the Guilford County Board of Commissioners (District 4) until 2020. Appointed to the North Carolina House, District 59, in April 2024 and won a full term that November. Lost re-election in 2026.
cands.gaps: We could not find his birthplace, where he grew up, or when he came to North Carolina. We found no documented positions on data centers or development, and no campaign statements or questionnaire answers. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey in 2020, 2022, 2024 or 2026. Ballotpedia lists sponsored bills but the list did not load, so we could not identify specific bills. We also found no notable endorsements or news controversies in the sources available.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Owner of a family trucking business. Served on the Guilford County Board of Commissioners (District 4), about eight years until 2020. Member of the NC House for District 59 from April 2024.
qual.why: He has held local elected office and about two years of legislative service, and has run a business. That puts him in the high range, below the top because his state legislative tenure is short and no chamber leadership is shown.

cands.name: Elma Hairston
cands.bio: Democrat who won the North Carolina House District 59 seat in Guilford County in 2026, defeating incumbent Republican Alan Branson. Motivational speaker, author, small business owner and nonprofit executive. Immediate past president of the High Point NAACP chapter.

endorsements.text: Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party (also listed: Lillian's List, Communication Workers of America NC, Sen. Gladys Robinson, the George Simkins Jr. Community PAC, and High Point council members Tyrone Johnson and Michael Holmes)
Ballotpedia lists the Progressive Caucus of the North Carolina Democratic Party, plus voter-guide recommendations from several Sway voting groups including NC Public School Champions

cands.gaps: We could not find where Elma Hairston was born or raised, or when she came to North Carolina. We found no record of earlier elected office. Her business and nonprofit roles come only from her campaign site, with no independent confirmation of the business name, her title or her tenure. We found no stated positions or past actions on data centers, property taxes, land buying, growth, immigration, policing, guns, abortion or school choice. Her site names only broad themes: healthcare, public schools, fair wages, housing aid and rent stabilization, responsible budgeting and corporate accountability. She did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no documented controversies or foreign ties.

qual.background: Her campaign site describes her as a small business owner and nonprofit executive. She is a motivational speaker and author and the immediate past president of the High Point NAACP. She has not held elected office before.
qual.why: Business ownership and executive experience put her in the middle band. No prior legislative service, law, policy or budget career is documented. Board and advisory seats are not counted.
